text.p: Following are some of the major events to have occurred on November 25 in history.
1783 - The last British troops left New York City at the end of the American War of Independence,
1844 - Karl Friedrich Benz, an engineer who built one of the earliest petrol-driven engines, born; his company eventually merged with Daimler to form Daimler-Benz.
1881 - Pope John XXIII was born as Angelo Giuseppe Roncalli; he became Pope in 1958.
1885 - King Alfonso XII of Spain died of tuberculosis aged 27.
1901 - Gustav Mahler conducted the world premiere of his "Fourth Symphony" in Munich.
1915 - Chilean General Augusto Pinochet born; he overthrew President Salvador Allende in 1973 and remained in power until he lost elections in 1990.
1923 - Mauno Koivisto, former president of Finland, born; he succeeded Urho Kekkonen in 1982 and had two terms as president.
1935 - King George II returned to Greece after 12 years of exile, restored to his throne by a referendum.
1936 - The Anti-Comintern Pact, an agreement between Japan and Germany to collaborate in opposition to the spread of Communism, was signed.
1941 - The British battleship Barham was sunk by a German U-boat off Sollum with the loss of 848 lives.
1952 - Agatha Christie's play "The Mousetrap" opened in London; still playing to audiences today, it holds the record for the longest continuous run of any show in the world.
1957 - Sir Ernest Oppenheimer, German-born industrialist and one of the leading players in the mining industry of southern Africa, died.
1965 - Concert pianist Dame Myra Hess, best known for her appearances in wartime National Gallery recitals in London, died.
1969 - Beatle John Lennon returned his MBE, awarded in 1965, to the Queen to protest at Britain's policy in Biafra and its support for the United States in Vietnam.
1970 - Japanese writer Yukio Mishima committed public ritual suicide in Tokyo, a protest against the westernisation of Japan and the weakness of its post-World War Two constitution.
1971 - Denmark and Norway became the first NATO members to establish full diplomatic relations with North Vietnam.
1972 - New Zealand's Labour Party was swept to power with a huge majority.
1973 - In Greece, military dictator George Papadopoulos was overthrown by rival officers in a bloodless coup.
1974 - The Irish Republican Army was outlawed in Britain following the deaths of 21 people in a pub bombing in Birmingham three days previously.
1974 - U Thant, Burmese diplomat, died; he became U.N. Secretary-General after the death of Dag Hammarskjold in 1961 and held the post until 1971.
1975 - Suriname achieved independence from the Netherlands.
1986 - John Poindexter resigned as U.S. national security adviser and Lt-Col Oliver North was dismissed from the National Security Council after the Iran-Contra scandal broke.
1992 - The Czech parliament voted to split the country into separate Czech and Slovak republics from January 1, 1993.
1993 - British author Anthony Burgess died.
1995 - Ireland voted to legalise divorce in the closest result in the nation's polling history, a margin of less than one percent.
